A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same transformer RLVR study. Their main text, figures, equations, and complete proof appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original synthetic state-tracking experiments over Z_96, with reward and attention-alignment learning curves in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: Section 7 retains these original synthetic experiments and their learning curves in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Both retain the same attention architecture, frozen atomic-skill MLP, terminal-reward REINFORCE objective, SFT comparison objective, and mixed-horizon update. Expanded setup explanations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate cyclic state tracking over Z_96 with fixed lengths 5, 15, and 45, and mixtures {5,15,45} and {5,35}. No additional evaluated tasks or domains appear in the appendices.

E2.justification: The reported experimental comparisons retain the same training configurations. SFT remains a theoretical comparison; the newly cited curriculum and prefix-based methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 7 retains uniform per-sample horizon sampling, batch size 512, greedy evaluation over 30 batches, and the same success and peak attention-hit metrics. No experimental setting changes are reported.

E4.justification: The fixed-horizon and difficulty-ratio comparisons test the same questions using the same evidence. No new ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses appear; the appendices retain their proof content.

E5.justification: The evaluation averaging practice is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-training-run or seed information, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 retain identical experimental plots. The findings remain that short fixed horizons learn, longer fixed horizons stall, the R=3 mixture learns through L=45, and L=35 remains near zero under R=7.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 replaces K=ceil(log_R(L_max/L_1)) with K=min{k:L_k=L_max}, correcting the recursive horizon sequence's endpoint indexing. The main theorem bounds and appendix proof arguments otherwise remain unchanged apart from notation and editing.

C1.justification: The new 'implicit curriculum' terminology foregrounds the easy-to-hard progression already described in v1. Both retain the short-horizon guarantee, long-horizon gradient barrier, spectrum-dependent relay/grokking dynamics, and Fourier-analysis contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a positional-shortcut explanation in Section 3.1 and arguments connecting broad difficulty spectra, filtering, and prefix-based exploration to the mechanism's applicability in Section 2. The existing relay explanation and substantive limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 7 retains the same implementation disclosures, including MLP pretraining and freezing, baseline momentum 0.95, and entropy penalty 10^-3. No new hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a curriculum and difficulty-aware RL paragraph and six references: Bae, Foster, Kordi, Narvekar, Qu, and Setlur and colleagues. This extends research context while retaining the existing closest-work and novelty comparisons.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, motivating question, introduction synthesis, and conclusion are extensively reframed around an implicit curriculum. Broad terminology and explanatory rewrites also affect the setup, learning-dynamics discussion, and experimental interpretation.

P2.justification: v2 groups Figures 2 and 3 together on page 16, whereas v1 separates them across pages 14–15. Figure 1 and Figure 3a captions are revised, while the underlying diagrams and experimental plots are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the horizon-indexing inconsistency in Section 5.1 and provides clearer explanations and additional curriculum-related context. These improve precision and readability, while the experimental evidence, main guarantees, proof arguments, and substantive limitations remain essentially unchanged.
